Per-study influence on the pooled result

Source: R/diagnostics.R
study_influence.Rd

Leave-one-study-out influence, via Pareto-smoothed importance sampling on the marginal likelihood, with optional exact refits for the studies PSIS cannot approximate. Answers "would this result survive without study i?".

Usage

study_influence(
  fit,
  refit = c("none", "flagged", "all"),
  k_threshold = 0.7,
  quiet = FALSE
)

Arguments

fit

A meta_did() fit.

refit

Whether to refit without studies PSIS flags. "none" (default) does no fitting and costs nothing. "flagged" refits once per study with khat above k_threshold. "all" refits once per study. Refits are expensive, especially with individual-level data, so nothing fits unless asked.

k_threshold

Pareto k above which a study is flagged.

quiet

Suppress the message naming how many refits will run.

Value

A data frame with one row per study: study_id, design, weight (the inverse-variance weight on the mean), info_loss (the precision about the pooled effect lost by dropping the study), elpd_i, khat, flagged, and — when refits ran — d_effect_mean, d_effect_sd and d_ci_width, the changes from removing that study.

Details

Two things are reported, and they are not the same:

  • weight is that study's inverse-variance share, from information_share(). It governs the pull on the pooled mean, and info_loss beside it is how much precision the fit loses without the study.

  • khat is the Pareto diagnostic from PSIS. It is formally a statement about whether the importance-sampling approximation is reliable, but it is elevated precisely when the leave-this-out posterior is far from the full one – so a high value means removing the study moves the posterior.

A low weight does not make a high khat ignorable. Weight describes the effect on the mean, while a discordant study acts on the between-study SD, and that widens every interval. In testing, the lowest-weighted study of thirteen (weight 0.069) doubled treatment_effect_sd and doubled the width of the pooled interval. That is why the refits report both.

PSIS runs on log_lik_marginal, which integrates out the study-level parameters. The conditional log_lik is unusable for this: a study's own theta is informed almost entirely by that study, so leaving it out makes the importance ratios heavy-tailed for every study regardless of influence (measured at 18 of 20 studies above 0.7 on a well-behaved fit). The marginal version is only available for configurations where the integral is exact — see shared_generated_quantities.stan — and this function says so rather than falling back silently.

See also

information_share(), sensitivity_trend()
